summary: Specifies a standard file format for YANG instance data. It documents data defined by YANG models at design time, at implementation time, or when no live server is available, following the syntax and semantics of existing YANG models and adding metadata.

eli5.summary: A file that saves a snapshot of network settings together with notes, so you can read it without a running device.

questions: how to store yang data in a file
how are yang instance data files named
what is a content-schema in yang instance data
what are the use cases for yang instance data files
subtitle: A standard file format for saving YANG-modeled data, with metadata, when no live server is around.

tldr.problem: Data defined by YANG models is often needed at design time, at implementation time, or whenever a live server is unavailable, but there was no standard way to store it in a file.
tldr.mechanism: A YANG instance data file holds one instance data set: a metadata header plus the content-data, encoded as XML or JSON using the existing YANG encoding rules.
tldr.outcome: Vendors, tools and operators can exchange documented server capabilities, default configurations and similar data as plain files. The RFC is a Proposed Standard.

today: RFC 9195 is a Proposed Standard published in February 2022 and has not been obsoleted or updated. The RFC expects other documents to define specific use cases for instance data.

sections.title: Why Instance Data Files
sections.content:
Data defined in YANG models is often needed when a live server is unavailable, for example at design time or implementation time. This RFC specifies a standard format for YANG instance data sets and instance data files. The format is defined by the ietf-yang-instance-data module, which conforms to the Network Management Datastore Architecture (RFC 8342).

The RFC lists eight already-implemented and potential use cases, including documenting server capabilities, preloading default configuration, documenting factory default settings, storing a device configuration for backup or audit, storing diagnostics data, and providing data examples in RFCs or Internet-Drafts. It deliberately does not limit future uses.
sections.eli5: Sometimes you need to know what a device can do before you have the device. A file with the answers solves that.

sections.title: Principles and Life Cycle
sections.content:
The design follows eight principles. Two formats are defined, based on the XML and JSON encodings. Existing encoding rules for YANG data are reused. A set can hold data for multiple modules, configuration data, state data or a mix, and partial data sets are allowed. The format works whether or not a server implements the module, and it can report which datastore the data belongs to.

An instance data set is created at one point in time. If the underlying data changes, the set no longer represents the current data unless it is updated. Current values can be fetched at runtime with NETCONF or RESTCONF, or received in YANG-Push notifications. Whether and how the data changes should be described in the set's description or in an implementation-specific way.
sections.eli5: A saved file is a snapshot. If the real thing changes afterwards, the snapshot gets out of date, so the label should say how often that might happen.

sections.title: The File Format
sections.content:
A file MUST contain a single instance data set and no additional data. The set has a header part carrying metadata and a content-data part, defined as an anydata node, carrying the data itself. The content-data MUST conform to the content-schema, with exceptions, MUST use UTF-8, and follows the XML encoding rules of RFC 7950 or the JSON rules of RFC 7951. It MAY also include metadata from RFC 7952, origin metadata, and implementation-specific metadata, which users MUST ignore if unknown.

Because partial data sets are allowed, the "mandatory", "min-elements", "require-instance true", "must" and "when" constraints MAY be violated. Configuration and operational state data MAY be mixed.

The header leaves include name, format-version, includes-defaults, content-schema, description, contact, organization, datastore, a revision list and a timestamp. Metadata MUST include the format version (the default applies if it is absent). It SHOULD include the name, the content-schema, a description and an indication of whether default values are included.
sections.eli5: Every file has a cover sheet with the title, author, date and what it is about, followed by the actual information inside.

sections.title: File Names
sections.content:
A file name SHOULD have the form instance-data-set-name ["@" (revision-date / timestamp)] (".xml" / ".json"). Examples from the RFC are acme-router-modules.xml and acme-router-modules@2018-01-25.xml.

If the name leaf is present, its value SHOULD be used in the file name. A revision date in the file name MUST match the leaf format and, if also in the header, MUST be the latest revision date inside the set. A timestamp in the name SHOULD equal the one in the header, with any colons replaced by underscores.
sections.eli5: The file name works like a label on a folder: what it holds and, if useful, when it was made.

sections.title: Specifying the Content Schema
sections.content:
To use a set properly, the reader needs its content-schema: the YANG modules, revisions, features and deviations the data is based on. It can be given in external documents or inside the set, using one of three methods.

  • Inline: the inline-yang-library node carries instance data of ietf-yang-library@2019-01-04 (RFC 8525), listing modules, features and deviations.
  • Simplified-inline: a list of module names with revision dates. This implies no deviations and all features supported.
  • URI: the same-schema-as-file leaf references another instance data file whose content-schema is reused. The file:// and https:// schemes MUST be supported. If the referenced file is unavailable, the content-schema is unknown.

The content-schema only records which modules were used to define the set. A server may support a different module set, so whether a set is usable with another schema depends on how much the two differ.
sections.eli5: The file says which rulebook it was written under, either by copying the rulebook in, listing its name, or pointing to another file that already says so.

sections.title: Examples from the RFC
sections.content: The RFC gives three worked examples. The first, an XML file named acme-router-modules@2022-01-20.xml, documents server capabilities and uses the inline method. The second, read-only-acm-rules@2022-01-20.xml, preloads default access control rules for a read-only role and uses the simplified-inline method. The third is a JSON diagnostics file that uses the URI method. It holds NETCONF server statistics produced every 15 minutes, so it carries a timestamp instead of a revision date.
sections.eli5: One file lists what a router can do, one holds ready-made rules for a read-only user, and one is a stats report that a router writes again and again.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The module only defines a wrapper structure and a metadata header, and the RFC does not specify any way to influence server behavior. The header is usually not sensitive, but a URI with a userinfo subcomponent or description text may be. The content may be sensitive, depending entirely on the content-schema, so files MAY need secure handling at rest and in transit, as for the result of a read operation returning the same data.

With the URI method, the referenced file could be altered maliciously or through normal handling, so the content-schema might differ from the one expected. Its integrity and stability should be protected.
sections.eli5: A saved file can hold private information, so guard it like the original. If it points to another file for its rulebook, make sure nobody swaps that file.

sections.title: Backwards Compatibility
sections.content: Backwards compatibility is not defined for instance data sets, since it depends on the use case and content-schema. For sets produced by design work, the RFC lists changes to avoid because they break the link between a list key and the managed entity: changing the key of an entry that represents the same entity, changing the meaning of an entry without changing its key, and reusing the key of a removed entry for a different entity.
sections.eli5: If you rename a student's ID number or give someone else an old ID, people get confused about who is who. Keep IDs steady.

viz.caption: THREE WAYS TO SPECIFY THE CONTENT-SCHEMA

items.title: Inline
items.text: Embeds YANG library data with revisions, features and deviations.

items.title: Simplified-inline
items.text: Lists module names and revision dates only.

items.title: URI
items.text: Reuses the content-schema of another instance data file.
